name: Temporal and Procedural Techniques
text:
# Temporal and Procedural Techniques


## Overview
This family encompasses techniques that generate volumetric data or manage rendering performance dynamically, rather than relying solely on static, pre-computed 3D textures [G]. It addresses the limitations of static data in terms of memory overhead, resolution limits, and interactivity [G]. The methods differ from standard [direct volume ray casting](#19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md) by either computing density analytically via [procedural noise functions](#1799-procedural-noise-functions.md) during the ray march [G], applying spatial distortions to rays for focus+context [G], modeling deformations via [inverse displacement](#10637-discontinuous-displacement-mapping-for-volume-graphics.md) mapping [G], or dynamically selecting between multi-frame rate warping and parallel raycasting based on workload complexity [G].

## Shared principles
The family shares the fundamental ray casting loop structure defined in [Direct volume ray casting](19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md), but modifies the sampling stage or the rendering pipeline control flow [G].

1.  **Procedural Evaluation**: Instead of sampling a fixed 3D texture, density $V(\mathbf{p})$ is computed on-the-fly using mathematical functions evaluated at the sample point $\mathbf{p}$ [G].
2.  **Dynamic Ray Trajectories**: Rays may be distorted or redirected based on lens parameters or displacement fields, requiring custom intersection logic with the volume bounding box [G].
3.  **[Adaptive Rendering](#18776-adaptive-rendering.md)**: The system may switch between rendering paradigms based on runtime metrics like resolution and sampling rate [G].

## Subtopics

### [Volumetric Smoke Rendering with Worley Noise and Light Maps](2447-volumetric-smoke-rendering-with-worley-noise-and-light-maps.md)
Uses 3D [Worley noise](#1726-worley-noise.md) for density generation and [light maps](#16885-light-map-l-map.md) for scattering. Chosen for real-time animated smoke effects where memory for high-res textures is prohibitive.

### [GPU-accelerated ray casting with volumetric lenses](6767-gpu-accelerated-ray-casting-with-volumetric-lenses.md)
Applies spatially varying ray distortions for focus+context. Chosen when visualizing specific regions of interest within large datasets without occlusion.

### [Procedural Volumetric Cloud Rendering (GPU Shader)](8240-procedural-volumetric-cloud-rendering-gpu-shader.md)
Evaluates procedural noise ([FBM](#1260-3d-perlin-like-noise-and-fractal-brownian-motion-fbm.md)/Worley) directly in the fragment shader. Chosen for infinite resolution clouds and seamless animation without [pre-computation](#2330-pre-computation.md).

### [Displacement Mapping for Volume Rendering](10659-displacement-mapping-for-volume-rendering.md)
Models interactive deformations (cuts, peeling) using inverse displacement mapping. Chosen for dynamic geometric changes without mesh re-tessellation.

### [Dynamic Multi-Frame Rate Rendering](11338-dynamic-multi-frame-rate-rendering.md)
Hybrid system switching between image-based warping and parallel raycasting. Chosen to optimize the trade-off between latency and quality based on current workload complexity.

## Background
The techniques originate from the need to render complex, dynamic volumetric phenomena and interactive deformations that cannot be efficiently stored in static voxel grids [G]. Procedural noise methods leverage the parallelism of GPUs to compute density analytically [G]. Lens techniques extend standard [projection models](#23322-camera-and-projection-models.md) to support interactive exploration [G]. Displacement mapping adapts surface modeling concepts to volume data for interactive editing [G]. Multi-frame rate rendering addresses the performance bottlenecks of high-resolution raycasting in distributed or multi-GPU environments [G].
